persons.name: Samuel Lewis

occupation.note: THE TRADE IS THE PAPER'S. The corpus reads it as music teacher, piano forte tuner, piano tuner, at the Democrat of 2 July 1834, column 29; the Democrat of 9 July 1834, column 1; the Democrat of 16 July 1834, column 1; the Democrat of 22 July 1835, column 5; the Democrat of 29 July 1835, column 8; the Democrat of 5 August 1835, column 4. The residents vocabulary's nearest period-correct word for it is `schoolteacher`, and where the corpus prints more than one trade they are all named here rather than reduced to the one the vocabulary could take.

persons.note: A DOCUMENTED PERSON, AND NOTHING ELSE IS CLAIMED. The papers name 'SAMUEL LEWIS' and 'SAMYEL LEWIS,' and 'Samuel Lewis' and give the trade; they do not say where this household lived, who else was in it, or when it came. So the record around this person carries nothing but the person: no dwelling, no division, no family, each written as unattested in its own block rather than filled in from the shape of the rest of the town. Cited at the Democrat of 2 July 1834, column 29; the Democrat of 9 July 1834, column 1; the Democrat of 16 July 1834, column 1; the Democrat of 22 July 1835, column 5; the Democrat of 29 July 1835, column 8; the Democrat of 5 August 1835, column 4. The corpus associates the name with South Water Street; that is where the paper does business with this person and not a statement about where they slept, and the storefront tickets are the ones that may stand a shop there. THE TOWN NEVER INVENTED A ROOF FOR THIS TRADE. The occupation census raised reconstructed households for the trades a town of 3,265 people needed and could not document; `schoolteacher` was not one of them, which is why this person could only ever be ADDED and never seated on an existing record — data/research/newspapers/register_1835.json calls it `new_resident` for exactly that reason. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). READ THROUGH A TRANSCRIPTION, not a scan: the owner's ruling of 2026-08-28 grades a transcription-mediated reading as documented, and the source record for the run states that standard and its limits. A scan read that confirms or corrects the name upgrades this entry.

resident_research.evidence_against: The surname 'Lewis' is in Fergus's death notices and no entry under it carries the initial 'S' of 'Samuel Lewis'. A surname-only agreement is a refusal, here as everywhere: the list prints eleven Smiths. The surname 'Lewis' stands on the Second Presbyterian roll and no line under it carries the initial 'S' of 'Samuel Lewis'. A surname-only agreement is a refusal. The surname 'Lewis' stands in the 1837 poll and no man under it carries the initial 'S' of 'Samuel Lewis'. A surname-only agreement is a refusal. The apparent hits are the FORENAME Lewis, not the surname — 'Burke, Lewis', 'Roberts. Henry Lewis' — and the volume prints no Samuel Lewis.
resident_research.summary: A plausible external identity for Samuel Lewis was found and is retained unasserted: no date, place, occupation or kinship discriminator bridges it to the 1835 person.
resident_research.notes: Repository lead retained as a candidate: Plausible, insufficient - and answerable without acquiring anything. 3 of the 5 card(s) heading 'Lewis' name Chicago or Cook County, the heading is the surname of Samuel Lewis exactly, and the cards under it cite andreas_history_of_chicago, which this project already holds. Read it there. No card here gives a forename, so this mints nobody. Research only. Later-volume readings are recorded here and NOT promoted: T-0513 consolidates and T-0514/T-0515 apply.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE NEWSPAPER REGISTER (T-0376), AND THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER RATHER THAN AN ARGUMENT. Every other record in this dataset argues for a household — a family the sources count, or a trade the town demonstrably needed. This one argues for a PERSON: the Democrat and the American name Samuel Lewis as a schoolteacher at Chicago 6 time(s), and this reconstruction did not hold them. `data/residents/` has no way to carry a person except inside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing: one member, no dwelling, no division, no origin, no arrival beyond the bound the paper sets. Reading a family, a house or a quarter of town into this record would be reading something the papers do not say. tools/mint_documented_residents.py derives the whole minted set and prints every candidate it refused, with the reason.
